newsitem.title: CHILE: Pinochet considering a seat in the Chilean Senate.
newsitem.headline: Pinochet considering a seat in the Chilean Senate.

text.p: Former Chilean military ruler Gen. Augusto Pinochet has said he might like to become a senator-for-life after his term as army commander-in-chief ends next year, El Mercurio newspaper reported on Sunday.
Under the constitution his own government wrote in 1980, Pinochet has a right to a lifetime seat in the Senate as a former president if he wants it.

"I've thought about becoming a senator-for-life, but it's not something I'm worrying about because when I retire I will devote myself to my grandchildren and to writing history," Pinochet said in an interview with El Mercurio.
If he took it, the seat could give the 81-year-old former dictator a prominent role in Chilean politics for years to come.

But Pinochet said President Eduardo Frei's unsuccessful efforts to abolish lifetime Senate seats and nine other non-elected Senate seats -- eight of which are currently held by military appointees -- was discouraging him from accepting the seat.

"I've thought about it, but what do I gain since it looks like the government is set on proposing a bill to eliminate the appointed and lifetime senators from the constitution? In my opinion that's a mistake," said Pinochet.

Pinochet said he might resign as army commander-in-chief a few months before his term expires in March 1998, happy to have saved his country from Marxism by ousting socialist president Salvador Allende in a bloody 1973 coup.

"I've served in every post a man can have, from sweeping bedrooms to commander-in-chief and president. Some criticise me, some don't. But many people know that if the military government hadn't existed, we would have had a Marxist government and experienced the backwardness that other countries have," he said.

"I feel that my period has ended and that I leave satisfied," said Pinochet, who has served as army commander-in-chief since turning the presidency over to civilians in 1990. "Perhaps I'll leave (the post) a week before, a month or three months before."
He gave the interview in the southern town of Coihaique during one of a series of what he called "farewell visits" to army bases around the country.
